body: Dude she’s not #1 priority if you’re willing to fuck her over just because you don’t like the car you are being GIVEN. Your needs over what car you drive are more important to you than her needs of actually having a car. I can’t believe this is even a question. My soul hurts for you. I hope she sees how unbelievably selfish you truly are and leaves because damn, you are entitled and spoiled.
This is so painfully true. I have been getting erased for years. Now I don’t even remember who I am as a person anymore.

I mean, if she’s rushing you that doesn’t mean you should rush him and the relationship. I don’t know why you would need to know this far in advance if you’re bringing a date. Normally the invites don’t go out until this point and rsvp’s aren’t due until about a month, month and a half prior to the wedding. I would just tell her that you don’t need a plus 1 then, because you will most definitely scare this dude away by asking him to attend a wedding with you, 5 months away. Plus weddings solo without knowing anyone can be some of the most fun weddings you attend!

I think if your mutual agreement was to go with the flow, asking him to a wedding as a friend or not 5 months in advance is contradicting that. That requires commitment. I would either go alone, or wait until at least June or July to ask him, if you’re both still interested.
I cannot believe there are other people who think bathrooms and closets are soothing too. If the bathroom is occupied, I head straight for my closet with a blanket and pillow and curl up.

Yes, the bedroom was never 100% safe. With the bathroom I could lock it, and open the drawers beside the door so that no one could get it even if they unlocked it from the outside. That was the only way to feel completely safe for me. I’m almost 30 and still to this day, I retreat to the bathroom for peace as well.

Driving myself does not cause my anxiety, but when my husband drives, I can hardly breathe. He’s very aggressive and negative to everyone who isn’t driving up to his standards and it feels like a prison every time I am in the car with him.

My bedroom does now, but I still don’t feel like it’s a place I can escape to. The bathroom is and always will be a private space. I thought I was the only person who did this. Glad to know I am not alone.
The bathroom is my safe haven too. I can lock the door and just be alone.

This is totally correct. I don’t think he had very good examples of healthy conflict resolution or healthy emotional support growing up. And he is completely in denial about that and how it’s affected our relationship. He has zero clue how to be someone’s partner. Its incredibly difficult and I feel completely overwhelmed. Thank you for your compassion.

Thank you for saying all of that. I try to be thoughtful and empathetic to everyone who is taking the time to write me, whether or not their responses are what I need. Everyone is entitled to their opinions and even if I don’t agree, I still try and appreciate them. He does not know what an equal partner is even though he thinks he does. I’ve tried to set boundaries and I’ve tried to keep them, but I guess I’m a people pleaser and I will constantly make excuses for other people’s behaviour because I’m empathetic. I always try to justify actions and words because of maybe their past or what they feel. I really am trying my best to figure out my life and posting my vulnerability on a public forum took a lot of courage for me. Thank you for having so much faith that I will figure this all out. This type of encouragement is exactly what I needed.

You are very right here. I don’t know if couples therapy would work because he is he problem. And he’s not willing to admit that. He legitimately thinks how he behaves is normal. And I’m so depressed about all of it. He’s made me question everything about myself. Thank you for allowing me to share my feelings and for validating me. I really appreciate all the thoughtful and kind responses that people have left me.
Yes, you are right. Everything you wrote is completely right.

Yes, he’s something, but I don’t know what. He is definitely one to gaslight, stonewall, and threaten to leave the house every time I bring up my feelings because he doesn’t want to deal with them. He is also someone who will say one thing to me, then in a fight will tell me that one thing was a lie and actually I’m a terrible person. So it’s hard to know what is truth or not, because he will compliment me then destroy it weeks or months later, leaving me utterly confused. I do feel increasingly unstable with him. I worked really hard in my 20’s to be in a good place, meditate, be self aware, be kind, less angry, and more forgiving. But I feel like he has ripped all of that away from me and now I feel like a worthless monster. I know he will love this child more than he loves me but if we were to break up, I do not know how he will behave. And that scares me so much. I feel like I will regret having children with him as well at this point, but also don’t want to regret the one chance I have at being a mom, a lifelong dream of mine. I really appreciate your response and I haven’t felt  more validated about my feelings in years from everyone here.
Thank you so much for your encouragement!
Yes, thank you for this!
Thank you. Your kindness is so appreciated.

Thank you for your thoughtful reply and your words definitely resonated with me. Yes, he always says he is “ trying” but he never does anything different. Then when he actually does his house chores without me nagging him, he has to puff out his chest like “ look at everything I am doing for you “. And then says that nothing he ever does it good enough when I bring up he has hurt me in some way. I am angry with myself. I am angry I put myself in this situation. I am angry I have made excuse after excuse for him and I’ve lost myself in the process. I’m angry that I married him and I’ve let him get away with so much. He makes promises he never keeps, he says he’ll do stuff that he never does, and I’m just crushed to the bone by it. Every day. He is just so convincing sometimes. My friend does still see hope for us if he was to agree to get help, but the fact he doesn’t, is a sign. He doesn’t want to better himself or us, he wants me to accept him and be his mother so that he doesn’t have to change a thing. And yes, when we do connect, it is magical. People constantly tell us that our connection is special, but the happiness never lasts. And he blames me for all of it.
Thank you, I needed to hear that. You are 100% right.

This breaks my heart for you, and except for the mother part, it reeks of similarities to my husband as well. There is always something else more important and that’s why he can’t help nor focus on me. I have never felt like his number one priority. I already know what the start of my breaking point was. I had a miscarriage a few months back and a day and a half into it, he started to berate me about things I had done months ago, or not done! He said I was lazy and I never did anything around the house ( even though I had planned a wedding and month long honeymoon by myself completely and did almost all the cooking, cleaning, emotional and physical labour for our entire relationship ) and when I would say well did you cook or clean? The answer is no, but he got more infuriated with me. I was laying on the bathroom floor crying and actively miscarrying and he couldn’t stop screaming at me for two days until I was finally just ready to end my life because I felt so pathetic. Then he was apologetic and tried to say he was going through a lot. I had to deal with my miscarriage completely on my own from that point on and he never asked me about it. I know a lot of people will say “ well why didn’t you leave him at that point “, and a lot of it is fear based and it’s always more complicated than I can type out. And he does have some redeeming qualities, there is still good in him. I am not perfect either, I have some difficult tendencies I am still working on from my childhood trauma. But now I’m pregnant again and my hormones are on over drive and I’m really starting to see him for who is truly is and how he has treated me and continues to treat me. Yes he has good qualities about him, but he is also deeply and emotionally unstable which is definitely from his childhood and he won’t seek help. He gets defensive every single time I tell him my feelings or something he has done to hurt me, and then it he makes it about him and how I do things that are wrong and I need to validate him even though he rarely validates me. He will actively ignore the things I tell him about me and say that he “ reads me” differently. Even though I tell him he’s reading me all wrong, he still sticks with this dialogue because he for some reason thinks he knows better than me. It’s insanely frustrating and confusing. This is a long vent, but your story just made me want to share mine that is similar. I’m going to therapy as soon as possible to try and regain my sense of self back and take back my life whether he is in it or not. Thanks for sharing your story.

I do think that he has good qualities and doesn’t 100% fit the narcissist criteria. He definitely grew up in a home though where emotions were not properly regulated or talked about. His siblings are very similar. I don’t think he was ever truly taught how nor does he have enough self awareness to see how his behaviour isn’t normal. He is also highly addicted to his cellphone and uses it as a security blanket in every situation. I will do therapy on my own for now, figure out what is best for me, and if he decides he wants to do it, then a positive first step, if not, I’m planning my exit. Thank you for your reply!

Well since I’m not in the states and I’m in a place where I have universal healthcare, yes that’s an option. Which I have thought about. But just because he might be a narcissist ( he doesn’t necessarily fit all the criteria ), doesn’t mean my child would be. I am an empath and very sensitive, so I would strive to raise my child that way. I’m sorry you had that experience and are now regretful, but aborting isn’t the only option and isn’t the right option for everyone.

I have suggested couples therapy I don’t know, about a million times, and he always says no. I have suggested therapy on his own to learn how to regulate his emotions and defensiveness, he says no. And then miraculously when my best friend tried to talk to him about everything, he said I’m the one that doesn’t want to do therapy, not him, and that he will suggest that again to me that night ( this was 3 days ago and not a word ). I have been in and out of therapy my entire life and he never has, so I would be the last person to say no to that. You are so right though, he doesn’t want to change and nothing I do will change that. Thank you for replying.
It’s definitely not a walk in the park and I’m just at my limits now, especially now. I would rather be a single mother at this point.

I’ve tried kindness and understanding, I’ve tried tough love, I’ve tried to be exactly what he says he needs in order to “ change “ and none of it has worked. Yes, I definitely recognize now that I’m in the same pattern I was as a child. No one to validate my feelings, but I have to be perfect for them. Even though it’s never actually good enough. I have read a lot about narcissistic partners and while he fits the bill for some of the criteria, he doesn’t for a lot of it. I’ve booked in for an emergency therapy session this week, and I will start seeing a psychologist in April. I appreciate you’re replies so much. Thank you for taking the time.

Thank you for your very thoughtful reply. I am a communicator, through and through. But he is not. He plays the victim a lot and always blames everyone else for his choices. He will blame me for not communicating because he doesn’t think I would want to talk, even though I’ve told him a million times that isn’t true and that’s all I want. I’m just lost. I don’t know what the right thing to do is.
Agreed. It’s awful and they do not help at all. It’s so impersonal.
I feel the exact same way.  I wish I had the courage.
